newsitem.title: BOSNIA: UN official threatened, beaten in Mostar, Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: UN official threatened, beaten in Mostar, Bosnia.

text.p: A United Nations official was assaulted and threatened at gunpoint by a man claiming to be a Croat policeman in the bitterly divided Bosnian town of Mostar, a U.N. spokesman said on Thursday.

Alva Emerson, U.N. coordinator for a joint Moslem-Croat police force in Mostar, was attacked on Wednesday evening after he tried to investigate an incident in which a relief worker was threatened in the Croat-controlled part of town, spokesman Alex Ivanko told reporters.

"They pointed at a man walking away and Emerson went after this person but was shown a (Croat) police badge. Then a gun was pointed at him and a round was chambered," Ivanko said. "We are now trying to confirm if he was a police officer or not."

Emerson, a U.S. citizen, followed the suspect to his house and tried to stop him when he came out again. In the ensuing fight, the U.N. official suffered "cuts to his right ear, bruises to his face and head and to the ribs", Ivanko said.
Emerson managed to hold the suspect and hand him over to the Croat police who took him into custody.
But police refused to provide the United Nations with the suspect's identity, Ivanko said, adding that the organisation was still investigating the incident.
A 10-month Moslem-Croat war in Bosnia devastated Mostar and left the ancient Ottoman town divided into Moslem and Croat sectors.
Thugs tolerated by Croat authorities have conducted a systematic campaign of expulsions of Moslems from west Mostar over the past year in blatant violation of the Bosnian peace agreement.
